The implementation follows the core of your PDF quite closely. I also found a few important gaps and one submission blocker that I'd fix before calling it ready.
Feature-by-feature audit
Legend: 
Implemented in code
 Partial / needs verification
 Blocker

Your Round 1 commitment	What I found in the repository	Verdict
F1. Versioned brand knowledge base	Versioned clauses, latest-version selection, pasted guideline import	Implemented
F2. Approved-facts registry	Facts are loaded into the engine and supplied to claim checks	Test actual matching
F3. Terminology enforcement	Banned terms, replacements and protected phrases are covered by tests	Implemented
F4. Multiple content formats	Text, Markdown, DOCX and PDF intake are described and wired into the application	Test each format
F5. Five MVP check groups	Six groups are declared in the Round 2 submission, including accessibility and channel rules	Implemented in design
F6. Evidence-backed findings	Retrieval-scoped clauses, exact quotations, content spans and severity mapping	Strong implementation
F7. Corrections as diffs	Accept, edit and dismiss actions; edits are human-controlled	Implemented
F8. Deterministic citation verifier	The review engine verifies candidate findings before saving them	Implemented
F9. Approval state machine	Role checks, legal transitions, blocker gating and self-approval restrictions	Implemented
F10. Comments, revisions and audit	Relevant actions and audit logging exist in the source	End-to-end verification needed
F11. Governance insights	Insights route and recurring-issue analysis are described and tested by the HTTP test script	Verify persistence and calculations
F12. AI disclosure	Disclosure page, engine mode and export disclosure are implemented in the stated design	Verify live output
F13. Visual and accessibility checks	Image metadata and accessibility checks are described in the engine and submission document	Check real uploaded assets
F14. Guideline-gap detection	Dismissal reasons and grouped gap candidates are part of the implementation	Verify the feedback loop
F15. Brand-health reporting	Trends and cycle-time metrics are included in the described build	Verify against real review data
F16. CMS integrations and bots	Explicitly deferred in your Round 1 plan	Correctly deferred

The core evidence and approval architecture is backed by actual source code, rather than only descriptions in the PDF. 
round1-submission (2)(2).pdf

The three most important problems
1. Critical: the repository is private
Fix before submission
GitHub's repository metadata confirms that ayushinn/codex48_ is currently private. Your event instructions require a repository link that judges can open without signing in.

Make it public, check that no secrets are committed, and test the link in an incognito window.



2. Personas are selectable by anyone
Security limitation
I inspected src/app/api/persona/route.ts. It lets a visitor set the persona cookie to any defined role without authentication. The approval API does check the selected role, which is good, but a visitor can choose Manager or Admin themselves.

This is acceptable as a clearly disclosed hackathon demo shortcut; it is not genuine user identity or secure role-based access control. Your Round 1 plan specified real authentication and server-enforced role permissions. Document this change honestly and use proper authentication and trusted role assignment for a production system.



3. Your submission document isn't ready to file
Incomplete paperwork
SUBMISSION.md still has placeholders for the team name, leader, project URL, repository URL and updated PDF path. Those need to be filled in.

The document also claims 12/12 unit tests and 35/35 HTTP checks. I inspected the test source, but I have not independently executed the test suite or confirmed those results against a live deployment.



Other implementation gaps worth knowing about
I also noticed a few nuances in the source:
- Guideline imports: src/app/api/knowledge/route.ts imports pasted text and classifies blocks into rule groups. The Round 1 plan also proposed importing brand books from PDF, DOCX and URLs. The Round 2 submission correctly records that guideline-file parsing is deferred.
- Fact verification: src/lib/engine/checks.ts uses a claim-pattern detector and token-overlap scoring to compare promotional claims against registered facts. That's a useful MVP heuristic, not comprehensive factual verification. It can miss claims that don't match its patterns or misclassify similar claims.
- Visual auditing: The engine accepts image metadata such as palette colours and contrast ratios. That supports a basic audit, but I haven't verified the browser-side measurements or whether they reliably represent the actual image.
- Persistence: The README explicitly warns that serverless deployments without DATABASE_URL may reset their embedded database on cold starts. Configure persistent Postgres before relying on saved reviews and audit history.
These are implementation observations from the repository, not claims that I have reproduced each issue in a running application.
What I'd do next, in order
Pre-submission checklist
0/7

[ ] Make the GitHub repository public and verify no secrets are exposed
[ ] Configure persistent Postgres for the deployed application
[ ] Test the complete review-to-approval-to-export journey
[ ] Test facts, terminology, guideline imports and real image uploads
[ ] Run npm run build, npm test and npm run e2e against the current code
[ ] Complete SUBMISSION.md and generate the updated Round 2 PDF
[ ] Verify the live app, repository and PDF in a private browser window

Final verdict
Yes, your codebase substantially follows your Round 1 product plan. The strongest alignment is in the deterministic evidence verifier, rule-based checks, human-controlled corrections, approval state machine and audit workflow.

I would not yet certify that the complete product works exactly as specified, because I haven't run it or tested the live application. And right now, the private repository alone conflicts with the explicit submission requirements.

The good news is that the next steps are specific. You don't need to throw away Preflight or redesign the entire product. You need to verify the working path, resolve access and persistence risks, and make the submission materials accurate.

    const match = version.match(/^\d+/);
    if (!match) {

    const releaseDateStr = NEXT_RELEASE_DATES[Number(match[0])];

### 3\. The most important technical findings

These are the things I would investigate or fix before spending time on additional features.

1\. Authentication and workspace isolation — highest priority

The README explicitly says no sign-in is required and a session cookie selects the active persona. That is useful for a frictionless demo, but it is not equivalent to the Round 1 plan's sign-in flow, secure sessions and enforced separation between real users.

The schema includes workspace IDs, but the reviewed database code does not establish the PostgreSQL row-level security promised in the PDF. Some API handlers also query reviews or select the first workspace without an obvious per-workspace authorization filter.

Why it matters: role checks can protect actions within the demo model without proving that one real customer cannot access another customer's content. Keep the demo simple, but don't claim production-grade authentication or isolation until this is addressed.

2\. Guideline import is narrower than planned

The knowledge API supports pasted guidelines, automatic clause classification, and version creation. That is a meaningful implementation of F1, but your plan specifically names PDF, DOCX, pasted text and public URL imports. Draft-file parsing does not automatically mean guideline-file importing works.

What I'd do: either implement guideline file import or clearly document that pasted guideline import is the Round 2 scope and file/URL imports remain future work.

3\. The review engine is explainable, but it is not a general-purpose semantic auditor

The inspected rules include regular-expression checks for banned terms and promotional claims, and lexical matching against registered facts. These are useful deterministic checks, but they can miss paraphrased claims or flag harmless wording. The optional LLM pass helps broaden coverage, but its presence depends on configuration.

The citation verifier is a good architectural choice. Still, verifying that a quote exists is not the same as proving that a finding is logically correct or that the cited clause actually supports the finding.

What I'd do: create a small labelled test set of genuine violations and clean content, measure false positives and false negatives, and show judges where the engine is reliable and where it needs human judgment.

4\. Image contrast is not yet a full WCAG contrast audit

The image-intake component calculates dominant colours and a contrast-related ratio. That is not equivalent to measuring the contrast between actual foreground text and its background. It also cannot establish logo clear space or approved logo usage merely from a palette.

What I'd do: label the current metric as an image-level heuristic, and only claim WCAG text-contrast validation if the product actually measures the relevant foreground/background pairs.

5\. Deployment persistence is a potential blocker

The database code falls back to embedded PGlite when `DATABASE_URL` is absent. The README itself warns that on serverless hosting this data lives in temporary storage and may reset on cold starts.

What I'd do: configure persistent PostgreSQL for the public demo, then test that reviews, decisions, audit entries and the seeded workspace survive refreshes and separate visits.

6\. Insights are a starting point, not yet the complete reporting promise

The insights page calculates useful groupings and trends. Dismissal clustering by normalized reason is a basic approach: two differently worded reasons with the same meaning won't necessarily land in the same cluster. The full plan also calls for suggested guideline clarifications, monthly reports and period-over-period comparisons.

What I'd do: keep the current dashboard for Round 2, but avoid claiming the full guideline-gap loop or complete brand-health reporting is delivered.

import { PGlite } from "@electric-sql/pglite";
import { drizzle as drizzlePglite, type PgliteDatabase } from "drizzle-orm/pglite";
import { neon } from "@neondatabase/serverless";
import { drizzle as drizzleNeon } from "drizzle-orm/neon-http";
import { randomUUID } from "node:crypto";
import { mkdirSync } from "node:fs";
import { sql } from "drizzle-orm";
import * as schema from "./schema";
import { BOOTSTRAP_STATEMENTS } from "./bootstrap";
import { seedDemoWorkspace } from "./seed";

export type DB = PgliteDatabase<typeof schema>;

/**
 * Dual driver, one schema:
 *  - DATABASE_URL set  -> Neon serverless Postgres (production, Vercel)
 *  - no DATABASE_URL   -> file-backed PGlite (zero-install local development,
 *                         and a functional ephemeral fallback in /tmp when the
 *                         app is deployed without a database configured)
 */
function createPglite(): PGlite {
  // Cloudflare Workers / some serverless runtimes have no durable filesystem.
  // In-memory PGlite still seeds a working demo per isolate.
  const forceMemory =
    process.env.PGLITE_MEMORY === "1" ||
    Boolean(process.env.CF_PAGES) ||
    Boolean(process.env.OPEN_NEXT_CLOUDFLARE);
  if (forceMemory) {
    return new PGlite();
  }
  const dir =
    process.env.PGLITE_DIR ??
    (process.env.VERCEL ? "/tmp/preflight-pglite" : `${process.cwd()}/data/preflight`);
  try {
    mkdirSync(dir, { recursive: true });
    return new PGlite(dir);
  } catch (err) {
    console.warn(
      "[preflight] file-backed PGlite unavailable, using in-memory:",
      (err as Error).message,
    );
    return new PGlite();
  }
}

function createDb(): DB {
  const url = process.env.DATABASE_URL;
  if (url) {
    const sqlClient = neon(url);
    return drizzleNeon(sqlClient, { schema }) as unknown as DB;
  }
  return drizzlePglite(createPglite(), { schema });
}

type Global = { db: DB; mode: "postgres" | "pglite"; ready: Promise<void> | null };
const g = globalThis as unknown as { __preflightDb?: Global };

async function bootstrap(db: DB, mode: "postgres" | "pglite"): Promise<void> {
  for (const statement of BOOTSTRAP_STATEMENTS) {
    await db.execute(sql.raw(statement));
  }
  await seedDemoWorkspace(db);
}

export function getDb(): { db: DB; mode: "postgres" | "pglite" } {
  if (!g.__preflightDb) {
    const mode = process.env.DATABASE_URL ? "postgres" : "pglite";
    const db = createDb();
    const entry: Global = { db, mode, ready: null };
    entry.ready = bootstrap(db, mode).catch((err) => {
      // allow retry on next access
      entry.ready = null;
      throw err;
    });
    g.__preflightDb = entry;
  }
  const entry = g.__preflightDb;
  if (entry.ready) {
    // awaited by callers through ensureDb()
  }
  return { db: entry.db, mode: entry.mode };
}

export async function ensureDb(): Promise<{ db: DB; mode: "postgres" | "pglite" }> {
  const { db, mode } = getDb();
  const entry = g.__preflightDb!;
  if (entry.ready) {
    await entry.ready;
  }
  return { db, mode };
}

/** Create a review and run preflight in one step (the judge's core path). */
export async function POST(req: Request) {
  const persona = await getPersonaFromCookie();
  if (!["creator", "admin", "manager"].includes(persona.role)) {
    return NextResponse.json({ error: `Role "${persona.title}" cannot create reviews.` }, { status: 403 });
  }

  const parsed = CreateReview.safeParse(await req.json().catch(() => null));
  if (!parsed.success) {
    return NextResponse.json(
      { error: parsed.error.issues.map((i) => `${i.path.join(".")}: ${i.message}`).join("; ") },
      { status: 422 },
    );
  }
  const input = parsed.data;

  const { db } = await ensureDb();
  const workspaces_ = await db.select().from(workspaces);
  const workspace = workspaces_[0];
  if (!workspace) return NextResponse.json({ error: "No workspace configured." }, { status: 500 });

  const channelList = await db.select().from(channels).where(eq(channels.workspaceId, workspace.id));
  const channel = channelList.find((c) => c.key === input.channelKey);
  if (!channel) {
    return NextResponse.json(
      { error: `Unknown channel "${input.channelKey}". Available: ${channelList.map((c) => c.key).join(", ")}` },
      { status: 422 },
    );
  }

  const id = randomUUID();
  await db.insert(reviews).values({
    id,
    workspaceId: workspace.id,
    title: input.title,
    channelKey: channel.key,
    contentType: input.contentType ?? channel.name,
    content: input.content,
    status: "DRAFT",
    createdBy: persona.name,
    images: input.images ?? [],
    engine: {} as never,
  });
  await logAudit(db, {
    workspaceId: workspace.id,
    reviewId: id,
    actor: persona.name,
    action: "review.created",
    detail: { channel: channel.key, chars: input.content.length, images: input.images?.length ?? 0 },
  });

  try {
    const summary = await runPreflight(db, id, { actor: persona.name });
    return NextResponse.json({ ok: true, id, summary }, { status: 201 });
  } catch (err) {
    return NextResponse.json(
      { ok: true, id, error: `Preflight failed: ${(err as Error).message}` },
      { status: 500 },
    );
  }
}

import { PGlite } from "@electric-sql/pglite";
import { drizzle } from "drizzle-orm/pglite";
import * as schema from "../src/lib/db/schema";
import { buildCtx, runRuleChecks } from "../src/lib/engine/checks";
import { attachContent, verifyCandidate } from "../src/lib/engine/verify";

const CONTENT =
  "AURORA CALM is here!!! Meet the #1 miracle ritual your mornings have been begging for.\n\nOur clinically proven formula guarantees results in 7 days - act now, limited time only! 94% of participants reported feeling more relaxed within 14 days.\n\n![image](spring-ritual-hero.jpg)\n\n[click here](https://aurorawellness.com/shop) to shop. Ships in 24 hours, anywhere in the world.\n\n#AuroraCalm #wellness #morning #selfcare #mindfulness #ritual";

async function main() {
  const db = drizzle(new PGlite("./data/preflight"), { schema });
  const allClauses = await db.select().from(schema.clauses);
  const terms = await db.select().from(schema.terms);
  const facts = await db.select().from(schema.facts);
  const channels = await db.select().from(schema.channels);
  const channel = channels.find((c) => c.key === "social")!;

  const t0 = Date.now();
  const ctx = buildCtx({
    content: CONTENT,
    channel,
    clauses: allClauses,
    terms,
    facts,
    toneExamples: [],
    images: [],
    palette: ["#1F3A2E", "#C9A227"],
  });
  const t1 = Date.now();
  const candidates = runRuleChecks(ctx).map((c) => attachContent(c, CONTENT));
  const t2 = Date.now();
  const verified = candidates.filter((c) => verifyCandidate(c, allClauses).ok);
  const t3 = Date.now();
  console.log("buildCtx ms:", t1 - t0);
  console.log("runRuleChecks ms:", t2 - t1, "candidates:", candidates.length);
  console.log("verify ms:", t3 - t2, "verified:", verified.length);
  console.log("total ms:", t3 - t0);
}

main();
"}}

process.env.DATABASE_URL = fs.readFileSync("DATABASE_URL.txt", "utf8").trim();

async function main() {
  const stale = await db
    .select({ id: schema.reviews.id })
    .from(schema.reviews)

  console.log("removing", ids.length, "probe reviews");
  if (ids.length) {
    await db.delete(schema.findings).where(inArray(schema.findings.reviewId, ids));

    await db.delete(schema.revisions).where(inArray(schema.revisions.reviewId, ids));

  const f = await db.select().from(schema.findings);
  console.log("findings remaining:", f.length);
}

main().catch((e) => {
  console.error("fatal", String(e?.message ?? e));
  process.exit(1);
});

## The live link works again — verified in incognito

**https://site-23a0517a0f274928a6afc55dce23e316.freebuff.page**

Two separate bugs were breaking it, not one:

1. **The demo database was left half-seeded.** A seed attempt had written the workspace row and then stopped, so the "already seeded?" guard skipped seeding forever — leaving the app with zero reviews. That's exactly what you saw disappear. The guard now keys on *reviews*, and a partial seed clears and rebuilds itself instead of staying broken ([seed.ts](src/lib/db/seed.ts)).
2. **Preflight spent its whole request budget on round trips.** Every new serverless isolate re-ran 15 bootstrap `CREATE TABLE` statements (~190 ms each to Neon), and each finding cost its own insert and delete. Requests were cut off mid-query — which is why *creating a review* 500'd on the deployed URL while working fine locally. Now the schema is probed instead of recreated ([db/index.ts](src/lib/db/index.ts)), and findings are written in one batched insert with one batched delete ([engine/index.ts](src/lib/engine/index.ts)). Creating a 13-finding review went from failing to **2.1s**.

## The judge journey on the live URL (not the dashboard)

Walked end-to-end in a private browser session, not just status codes:

- **New review** → planted-violations draft → Run preflight → **13 findings, 9 blockers**, each with severity, why, verbatim clause quote (GB-1.1, GB-2.1, GB-2.2, GB-3.1, GB-4.1, GB-4.2, GB-5.1), and a diff.

- **Dismiss with reason** → typed a reason, blockers 8 → 7, "finding dismissed" in the append-only audit log.
- **Creator → Manager handoff** on the seeded newsletter: switched persona, *Take into review* (In review), *Approve* (Approved), *Mark publish-ready & export*.
- **Export** returned the approval record with the full trail (`submit → take_review → approve → mark_publish_ready`, each with actor and timestamp) and the AI-disclosure footnote.
- **Insights** loads with recurring issues by clause, dismissal rate, median cycle time and gap candidates.

Then I reseeded the hosted DB so those test approvals don't leave the demo in a used state — it's back to the five seeded reviews (4 publish-ready/review states + 1 self-review), 29 findings.

## Requirement 3 — clean-db

[package.json](package.json) now runs `tsx scripts/clean-db.ts` with **no `--confirm`**, so the script's own guard is genuinely explicit. It also still refuses to run when `DATABASE_URL` is set or `DATABASE_URL.txt` exists, so it can't touch the hosted database.

`npm run typecheck` clean · `npm test` **14/14** · `npm run build` clean · `npm run e2e` **35/35** · all live routes 200 (0.5–2.3s) · incognito dashboard shows 5 reviews with `DB: postgres`.
